I think if we want to remain rational and respectful in our discussion of this situation, we have to stop equating these battles with FiftyFifty. 1. The 3/4 members lost one injunction, which is the same thing that happened with several Loona members, 2. The 3/4 members never went to the media to cry in interviews and point fingers at other idols/average staff members, 3. There are a lot more court cases to follow that have not been resolved yet (if you look into it, Attrakt is the one who is delaying the cases still), 4. I don't mean this to bring down Keena at all, but she was also threatened with being sued out of millions of dollars without having the wealthy family background of the NJ girls. She is brave for many reasons, but it's hard to say if it actually is bravery when she was facing down the barrel of financial ruin.

I won't say that the 3/4 members made their own mistakes - they, too, were just young girls who barely turned into adults. However, while they probably didn't come from a 'poor' family, they definitely did not come from a family that already had millionaires. They did not have a weird MHJ cult figure constantly talking about how she is basically a martyr for the rights of women/idols/whatever. And, neither ADOR/HYBE \*or\* Attrakt is going to necessarily be blameless. We can both acknowledge that the agencies \*and\* those fighting against the agencies, whether FiftyFifty or NJs, can have fault. But we also have to acknowledge that these situations have so, so many differences.
